title: Formal laws for the categorical trace
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber] and coefficient conventions [def-trf-coefficient-conventions], with $A=A_{E,n}$. Use the categorical trace of [def-trf-categorical-trace] on perfect ordinary module complexes [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex], and its same signed dual-frame construction over any commutative coefficient ring. In this proposition $D^b_{\mathrm{fin}}(A)$ means $\operatorname{Perf}(A)$, as in that trace definition; it does not mean all complexes with finite cohomology. For a field $F$, $D^b_{\mathrm{fin}}(F)=D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(F)$ has bounded finite-dimensional cohomology [def-weil-point-fd-complexes]. For $\Lambda=\Qlb$, in the common-stage notation [def-weil-point-fd-qlbar-category]: compute the endomorphism, cohomology and scalar trace at a common finite coefficient-field stage and extend scalars to $\Qlb$.

1. Conjugacy invariance. For perfect $P_1,P_2$ and endomorphisms $v_i$ in $D(A)$, if $w:P_1\xrightarrow{\sim}P_2$ satisfies $v_2\circ w=w\circ v_1$, then $\operatorname{tr}_A(v_1\mid P_1)=\operatorname{tr}_A(v_2\mid P_2)$.
2. Filtered additivity. Suppose $P'\to P\to P''\to P'[1]$ is a distinguished triangle of perfect complexes and $(v',v,v'')$ has filtered origin: the triangle and these endomorphisms are induced by a pair of complexes $K'\subset K$ and an endomorphism in the category obtained by inverting filtration-preserving quasi-isomorphisms on both $K'$ and $K/K'$ in the filtered homotopy category. Then $\operatorname{tr}_A(v\mid P)=\operatorname{tr}_A(v'\mid P')+\operatorname{tr}_A(v''\mid P'')$. In particular this applies to a filtration-preserving chain endomorphism of a short exact sequence of bounded finite-projective complexes. The corresponding assertion for arbitrary endomorphisms of Verdier distinguished triangles is false: over $R=\mathbf Z/4$, the triangle from $0\to R[-1]\to[R\xrightarrow{2}R]\to R\to0$, with middle endomorphism $(0,2)$ in degrees $0,1$ and zero endomorphisms on the ends, has middle trace $-2\neq0$ (Stacks Tag 087J).
3. Scalar extension. For any ring homomorphism $\rho:A\to B$ of commutative rings, any perfect $P$ and its endomorphism $v$, the extended complex is perfect and $\rho(\operatorname{tr}_A(v\mid P))=\operatorname{tr}_B(v\otimes_A^LB\mid P\otimes_A^LB)$, where $-\otimes_A^LB:D(A)\to D(B)$ is the total left derived functor [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] of termwise extension of scalars along $\rho$ [def-weil-module-base-change].
4. Supertrace over a field. For $\Lambda\in\{E,\Qlb\}$, $P\in D^b_{\mathrm{fin}}(\Lambda)$ and $v:P\to P$, $\operatorname{tr}_\Lambda(v\mid P)=\sum_{i\in\mathbf Z}(-1)^i\operatorname{Tr}(H^i(v)\mid H^i(P))$.

proof.text: For conjugacy use the canonical Koszul braiding and the right dual of each perfect complex. MonoidalCategory.trace_eq_of_iso proves equality of the two endomorphisms of the tensor unit. Applying perfectTraceScalar gives the scalar identity.

proof.text: The coefficient ring A=O_E/(uniformizer^n) is either the zero ring or a quotient of the local discrete valuation ring O_E, hence local. In the zero case every module is free. Otherwise a finite projective A-module is finite flat and therefore free by Mathlib Module.free_of_flat_of_isLocalRing. Choose bounded projective representatives from perfection and use the K-projective full-faithfulness theorem to lift a derived endomorphism to a chain map. On the resulting finite free model the already proved source-library trace_eq_algebraMap_sum_negOnePow_linearMapTrace computes the same signed dual-frame categorical trace. Evaluating the scalar endomorphism of the unit at one recovers its coefficient.

proof.text: Apply exists_filteredProjectiveModel to the filtered derived object and its endomorphism. Its two graded pieces are bounded finite projective and, by the preceding local-ring argument, degreewise finite free. The proved source-library trace_eq_trace_add_trace_of_shortExact applies to the model short exact sequence and its compatible chain endomorphism. The localization factorization identifies its total map, and the model isomorphism identifies both graded maps. Apply the additive function perfectTraceScalar to the categorical trace equation. This retains the filtered-origin hypothesis throughout.

proof.text: Construct M=[Z/4 --2--> Z/4] explicitly with HomologicalComplex.double. Multiplication by two squares to zero, so the components (0,2) define a chain endomorphism. Construct the inclusion from the degree-one single complex and projection to the degree-zero single complex; evaluation in every degree proves their short exactness. The composite of the inclusion with the endomorphism is null-homotopic, with the identity from degree one to degree zero as homotopy. The other composite is strictly zero. Mathlib triangleOfSES is distinguished, and these equalities define its endomorphism (0,w,0). The finite free chain trace formula gives 0-2=-2, which is nonzero in Z/4.

proof.text: For an arbitrary universal derived scalar extension LF, a bounded finite free model is K-flat by acyclic_mapBifunctor_of_boundedAbove_flat. Its scalar-extension counit is therefore invertible. Compose the homotopy-quotient comparison, the counit, and the termwise-extension comparison to identify LF(P) with the scalar-extended model. Counit naturality gives the required equation on endomorphisms. Extended terms are again finite free and bounded, proving perfectness. The proved source-library exists_trace_eq_algebraMap_and_trace_extendScalars_eq_algebraMap computes the two categorical traces as the images of one scalar; perfectTraceScalar recovers that scalar on either side. No flatness of the target ring is assumed.

proof.text: For a field F, use only the perfectness conclusion of field_complex_cohomology_splitting for an object with bounded finite-dimensional cohomology. Choose a bounded finite projective model and chain representative as above. All vector spaces are free. The proved source-library Hopf trace theorem sum_negOnePow_smul_trace_f_eq_sum_negOnePow_smul_trace_homologyMap identifies the finite signed chain trace sum with the finite signed homology trace sum. The natural isomorphism homologyFunctorFactors transports these endomorphisms to H^i(P); LinearMap.trace_conj' preserves each trace. Outside the model interval the term and therefore its homology are zero, so finsum_eq_sum_of_support_subset identifies the finite sum with the displayed finitely supported sum.

source.place: Clauses (1)--(4), implemented using the adopted source-library trace calculations

proof.text: For a common-stage object take t to be the categorical trace of its actual realization in D(Omega); exact field scalar extension preserves bounded finite-dimensional cohomology, so this object is perfect. For any finite-stage presentation, the termwise scalar-extension comparison is invertible. Apply the preceding finite-free scalar trace calculation and conjugacy along the realized presentation isomorphism to obtain its scalar trace t. The field Hopf trace formula gives its cohomological supertrace as the same t. For uniqueness, HomSurj of pointFdQbarCocone_isFilteredTwoColimit represents v at one common finite stage. Since the two structure arrows from the same original field are equal, its comparison isomorphism intertwines that representative with v. Evaluate the asserted property for t and any competing scalar on this presentation. Their scalar traces coincide, proving uniqueness without asserting equivalence with all of D(Omega).
